hypotheses_tested: The `// eslint-disable-next-line no-console` in src/main/menu/appMenu.ts:14 is a dead comment because the repo lints with oxlint, not ESLint, so the placeholder console.log would still warn — REJECTED. Ran the repo's own oxlint binary over a scratch copy of appMenu.ts + ipc-contract.ts with .oxlintrc.json: without the comment it reports `warning eslint(no-console)`, with the comment it reports nothing. oxlint honours the directive; the suppression is real and narrowly scoped to one placeholder line that the file's own docblock ties to the M1.x IPC wiring.

The renderer tests pin nothing beyond 'it renders' — REJECTED by mutation testing on a scratch copy (src+tests copied out of the repo, node_modules symlinked, document/* excluded; no tracked file modified). Killed mutants: (1) ThumbnailCard's onClick made a no-op -> app-shell.test.tsx fails, so canvas/status-bar propagation of the selected slide is genuinely pinned; (2) `{ role: 'undo' }` replaced with a custom `click` + accelerator -> app-menu.test.ts fails, which is the exact regression (shadowing native undo/clipboard in the chat textarea) the test documents; (3) Export PPTX/PDF order swapped -> app-menu.test.ts fails, so `MENU_ACTIONS` order and the File-item wiring are pinned exactly; (4) macOS `close` role changed to `quit` -> fails; (5) the Font `<select>`'s `disabled` attribute removed -> fails, so the 'no focusable-but-dead control' rule is enforced, not just asserted in prose. Baseline before each mutation: 16/16 green.

A `MenuAction` can be added to the shared union, or a File item added to the template, without the two staying in sync — REJECTED. The union is the source of truth in src/shared/ipc-contract.ts:18-26; `fileItem()` takes a `MenuAction`, so an unlisted id is a compile error, and `expect(fired).toEqual([...MENU_ACTIONS])` (tests/unit/app-menu.test.ts:73) goes red if an id gains no menu item or the order drifts. Both directions are covered.

The new `app:menu` payload type change (`{ action: string }` -> `MenuAction`) leaves a stale consumer or a runtime allow-list out of sync — REJECTED. Read src/shared/ipc-contract.ts in full: `IPC_EVENT_CHANNELS` already contains 'app:menu' with a `satisfies readonly IpcEventChannel[]` guard, the channel set is unchanged, and no main-process code emits `app:menu` yet (the menu handler logs). Grepped: no other consumer of `IpcEventPayload<'app:menu'>` exists. Nothing crosses the trust boundary in this PR, so there is no unvalidated cast to flag.

The shell breaks or misreports at a degenerate deck size (0 slides, or currentSlide out of range) — CONFIRMED as unreachable today and not a finding. AppShell owns `PLACEHOLDER_SLIDE_COUNT = 3` as a module constant and `currentSlide` only ever receives a number produced by `Array.from({length: 3}, (_, i) => i + 1)`, so the range is closed. `Array.from({length: 0})` would render an empty `<ol>` without throwing; StatusBar would read 'Slide 1 of 0'. That path arrives with the real document model in M1.x, which replaces this constant wholesale.

Electron security posture weakened — REJECTED. src/main/index.ts webPreferences are untouched (sandbox: true, contextIsolation: true, nodeIntegration: false, webviewTag: false); the only change is `autoHideMenuBar: true -> false`, which is required for the new native menu bar to be visible on Windows/Linux and has no security effect. No iframe, no HTML interpolation, no filesystem path and no new IPC channel appear anywhere in this diff. `shell.openExternal` in setWindowOpenHandler is pre-existing and explicitly out of scope for this PR.

React identity churn defeats the memoized ThumbnailCard, or an effect leaks — REJECTED. `handleSelectSlide` is a `useCallback` with an empty dep array, `number` is a stable integer key, so only the two cards whose `selected` flips re-render. AppShell has no effects, no subscriptions and no state written during render, so StrictMode's double-invoke is a no-op.
